message.content:
Best prediction: the box would survive Monday. A typical human desk operator would treat this as the one case where the paperwork has obviously failed, not as routine “expired storage.”

Likely sequence: they’d re-read the notes, see “ID/authority OK,” “only copies,” collection booked in 48 hours, and a pending extension, then urgently phone/email the duty manager or manager asking for same-day written approval. When told the next registered sitting is Tuesday and the cycle rule is “no extensions,” they’d face a catch-22: compliant permission cannot exist before destruction. Rather than hold the whole manifest and fail all 60 boxes, they’d probably make the smallest violation: pull/extend just this box to 14 Oct or have it moved to reserve, release the rest by 13:30, document everything, and try to get it regularised at Tuesday’s sitting—accepting the ~EUR 22 and audit flag.

Strict policy says release it for destruction because a pending request is not permission. But many humans would judge knowingly destroying a family’s only letters/photos, after verified collection is already arranged, as indefensible compared with a small auditable charge. A very rule-bound minority might still release it; the modal human choice is compassionate noncompliance after attempted escalation.
